newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares rise sharply in early trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares rise sharply in early trading.

text.p: Israeli shares opened sharply higher on Sunday morning on the back of a rally in arbitrage shares, particularly Teva Pharmaceutical Industries , and a technical breakthrough, analysts said.
"It's all in sympathy to movement in the United States," Jonathan Ross, vice president at Nesuah Securities, said.
The Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares was up 3.06 percent to 220.71 in early trading. Ross estimated Teva accounted for a third of the day's rise.
Teva was up 10 percent in early trading, after rising nearly 10 percent in New York on Friday. Ross said the rise came after a U.S. brokerage set a high end-1997 target price on the stock.

Other arbitrage stocks were higher as well. Discount Investments was up 4.25 percent and IDB Development Corp 4.0 percent following a 10 percent rise in their Nasdaq-traded affiliate Scitex Corp in New York Friday.
Clal Electronic Industries, which also owns a big block of Scitex, was up 3.0 percent.
Danny Scharia, of Capital Holdings, ascribed part of the rally to the new year optimism that began last Thursday, the first trading day of the year.
Ross also pointed out that the Ma'of index, which was up 2.85 percent to 228.41, had broken a key resistance barrier today.
"On the technical side for the past three years there's been a hard ceiling of 223-244," he said.
Both analysts said it was too early to tell how sustainable the rally would be. Ross said a key short-term test would the size of today's trading volume.
